title: Connecting to Atlas
idea: MongoDB Atlas is MongoDB's hosted service. Your code connects to it with the same `connectDB`; only the `MONGO_URI` value changes.
points: Atlas needs a database user, which is separate from your Atlas login.
Atlas accepts connections only from addresses on the project's IP access list.
Atlas gives you a `mongodb+srv://` string; store it in `.env` as `MONGO_URI`.
`dbName` still picks the database; the Atlas string names none.

parts.label: Scheme
parts.note: `+srv` looks the cluster's hosts up in DNS and turns on TLS, encryption in transit, by default.

parts.label: Database user
parts.note: Created in Atlas for your app. It is separate from your Atlas login.

parts.label: Password
parts.note: Percent-encode reserved characters such as `@`, `/` and `:` before pasting it here.

parts.label: Cluster host
parts.note: The `@` ends the credentials. Atlas assigns the host name; yours will differ.

parts.label: Database path
parts.note: Atlas leaves it empty. `dbName` in `connectDB` picks the database.

parts.label: Options
parts.note: `retryWrites=true` retries certain failed writes once. `w=majority` waits until most replica set members confirm a write.

code.title: Encode the password
code.caption: `URL` shows how reserved characters split a string. The driver needs them percent-encoded too.

walk.text: Demo values. A real password containing `@`, `/` or `:` breaks a raw URI.
Unencoded, the `/` ends the host part early, so the host reads as `ss`.
`encodeURIComponent` turns each reserved character into `%` and two hex digits.
Encoded, the host is right, and decoding returns the original password.

pitfalls: Keep `MONGO_URI` in `.env` and out of Git: it contains a live password.
Percent-encode reserved characters, such as `@` and `/`, in the password before building the URI.
When a connection times out, check that your current IP address is on the access list.

quiz.why: `encodeURIComponent` turns `@` into `%40` and `:` into `%3A`. Atlas passwords need the same treatment.

takeaway: Atlas changes the `MONGO_URI` value, not your connection code.

starters: What does `+srv` change compared with a plain `mongodb://` string?
Why is a database user different from my Atlas login?
Can I use a local MongoDB in development and Atlas in production?
